clauses.clause: Use a variety of communication modes to share information.

verdicts.evidence: Cold call on two to three students to share out details of what they see. … Cold call on one to two students to share out. … Cold call on two to three students to share out. … Refocus students whole group and call on a few students to share out.
verdicts.rationale: Students share relevant and accurate information through multiple communication modes. In Work Time A, students share details about the setting ('dark sky, people and animals down below'), Moon's experiences ('beautiful things such as children dreaming, foxes, flowers blooming, fireworks'), and their reasoning about Moon's decision, with the teacher cold-calling students to share out. In Work Time B, students role-play the characters and setting. In Work Time C, students write about characters and setting on the response sheet. In Closing, students share their sun/moon preference with partners and whole group. The variety of modes—partner talk, whole-group oral sharing, whisper responses, written responses, and role-play—satisfies all three clauses.

clauses.clause: Make use of texts to build knowledge, develop skills, make informed decisions, and/or share information and ideas. (I/C) [OR-list: any one student-performed purpose suffices for full]

verdicts.evidence: Invite students to turn and talk with an elbow partner: 'Based on the illustrations for evidence, what did Moon see when he paid attention to the world during the night?' (beautiful things such as children dreaming, foxes, flowers blooming, fireworks, etc.)
verdicts.rationale: The standard 1.P.EICC.2.b requires students to make use of texts for any one of four interchangeable purposes (build knowledge, develop skills, make informed decisions, share information and ideas). Throughout the lesson, students actively use the text Sun and Moon to build knowledge: they turn and talk to answer questions about characters and setting ("Who are the characters in this story?"), use illustrations as evidence ("Based on the illustrations for evidence, what did Moon see when he paid attention to the world during the night?"), and discuss why Moon changed his mind. Students also share information and ideas during the Closing structured discussion ("Would you rather be the sun or the moon? Why?"), drawing on the text. Because the student performs at least one listed purpose — building knowledge from the text — the OR-list clause is fully met.
